children: Refining and marketing swings back into profit in Q2, offsetting softer production and supporting ONGC’s quarterly earnings recovery

Oil and Natural Gas Corporation (ONGC) reported a 46.9 per cent year-on-year increase in consolidated net profit to Rs 18,534.82 crore in the second quarter of FY27; the growth is linked to a sharp improvement in the ONGC's refining and marketing segment and higher oil and gas realisations. The quarterly performance comes against a modest 3.8 per cent rise in consolidated profit for the first half of the financial year.

Consolidated revenue from operations increased 25.6 per cent to Rs 1,98,263.33 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 1,57,913.60 crore a year earlier. However, consolidated net profit for H1 FY27 stood at Rs 25,089.26 crore, compared with Rs 24,168.81 crore in the year-ago period. Profit attributable to owners rose 55.3 per cent to Rs 16,743.54 crore in Q2 and 39.1 per cent to Rs 28,642.47 crore in H1.

The refining and marketing segment emerged as a key driver of the quarter. The segment reported a profit before tax and interest of Rs 9,806.81 crore in Q2, compared with a loss of Rs 16,154.95 crore in the June quarter and a profit of Rs 6,526.15 crore in Q2 FY26.

The swing in quarterly segment profitability helped offset weaker performance in some other businesses. The exploration and production (E&P) business remained profitable, with the offshore segment reporting a result of Rs 12,358.43 crore and the onshore segment reporting Rs 3,963.30 crore in Q2. Petrochemicals, however, remained in loss at Rs 240.54 crore.

The improvement in refining and marketing also changes the picture between the two quarters. In Q1, the segment reported a loss of Rs 16,154.95 crore, which contributed to the relatively weak consolidated performance in the first half. The Q2 recovery brought the segment back into positive territory.

ONGC also benefited from stronger hydrocarbon realisations. Its nominated crude oil realisation increased 37.1 per cent to USD 92.33 a barrel in Q2 FY27 from USD 67.34 a barrel a year earlier. The price for nomination gas increased 3.7 per cent to USD 7.00 per million British thermal units, while the price for new-well gas rose 22.5 per cent to USD 10.24 per million British thermal units.

The improvement in realisations came even as ONGC recorded lower production. Standalone crude oil production declined to 4.437 million tonnes in Q2 FY27 from 4.630 million tonnes a year earlier. Natural gas production fell to 4.839 billion cubic metres from 4.918 billion cubic metres.

ONGC attributed the production moderation to reservoir behaviour in the KG-98/2 asset in the Eastern Offshore Basin, monsoon-related operational challenges and delays in pipeline replacement projects. Lower customer offtake also affected gas production from some onshore fields.

The company is responding to the production pressure through higher development activity. ONGC has awarded two Western Offshore development projects worth about Rs 11,800 crore, which are expected to unlock an estimated 22 million tonnes of oil equivalent of hydrocarbon potential.

The company has also expanded the engagement of bp as a technical service provider for the Western Offshore and awarded Pipeline Replacement Project-X at an estimated cost of more than Rs 4,300 crore.

ONGC’s board has also approved an interim dividend of Rs 8 per equity share, or 160 per cent of the Rs 5 face value. The total payout will amount to Rs 10,064 crore, the company’s highest-ever dividend paid in a single instalment.
